description: Removes clicks from the START and/or END of a file by TRIMMING: material outside the first/last sustained signal above `gate` is cut away (the file gets shorter - this is a trim, not a de-clicker). Both trim flags default ON in this entry; CDP REFUSES a flagless call ('Input file will be UNCHANGED.', exit 255). Verified on a click-silence-body-silence-click fixture: -b -e cuts to 1.8867 s from 2.0 with both clicks gone (head max 0.0); on near-flat noise the trim is negligible (1.9849 from 2.0, -0.75% - the static model's regime). The trim amount is CONTENT-DEPENDENT: how much low-level material precedes/follows the real signal. Certain gate/content combinations abort verbatim 'At this gate level and splice length, entire file will be removed.' (observed with -b alone on the click fixture). Deterministic; mono and stereo accepted (stereo verified, same arithmetic).
musical_use: The take-cleaner: strip the record-button click, the headphone spill before the downbeat, or the thump of the stop from every captured take before it enters a processing chain - clicks at file edges otherwise survive EVERY downstream process and reappear at full level after normalisation. Run it as takes' first stop; the splice eases the new edges so the trim itself cannot click. gate is the sensitivity: low values (0.01-0.05) only remove near-silence and spikes, higher values eat into quiet intros - if a piece genuinely fades in, trim only the end (trim_start false). For interior clicks use housekeep deglitch; for shaped fades after trimming, envel dovetail.

gate.description: Level ABOVE which signal is accepted as real (enforced 0-1 verbatim: 'Parameter[1] Value (1.500000) out of range (0.000000 to 1.000000)'). Everything before the first / after the last accepted signal is trimmed. Breakpoint file refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.'). Required.

splicelen.description: Splice length in milliseconds applied at the trimmed edges (enforced 0-200 verbatim: 'Parameter[2] Value (-5.000000) out of range (0.000000 to 200.000000)'). Breakpoint file refused ('Cannot read parameter 2 [...]'). Required.

trim_start.description: Trim the start (default ON here: CDP refuses a call with neither flag - 'Input file will be UNCHANGED.'). Set false to protect a genuine fade-in.

trim_end.description: Trim the end (default ON here). Set false to protect a natural decay.

examples.description: Clean both ends of a captured take.
examples.expected_use: Edge clicks and surrounding near-silence removed (verified head max 0.0); output slightly shorter than the input, edges spliced.

examples.description: Trim only the tail, preserving a quiet intro.
examples.expected_use: Start untouched; end trimmed back to the last signal above 0.05.

known_issues: This is a TRIM: output duration = indur minus the content-dependent trimmed spans. The static model is the near-flat-material bound (-0.75% on flat noise); on padded takes the shortening equals the padding (verified -0.11 s on the click fixture).
At least one of -b/-e is required: a flagless call refuses 'Input file will be UNCHANGED.' (exit 255) - both default ON in this entry.

Gate/content combinations that would delete everything abort verbatim: 'At this gate level and splice length, entire file will be removed.' (observed with trim_start alone on a fixture whose body followed a long quiet stretch).
Both numeric parameters reject breakpoint files ('Cannot read parameter N', N = 1-2). splicelen enforced 0-200 ms.
Deterministic (identical decoded shas 1.2 s apart); stereo verified.
